To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the exposure of the brain of laboratory rats to millimeter electromagnetic radiation modulated as a low-frequency pulse series leads to a suppression or inhibition of the development of an avoidance conditioned reflex with painful reinforcement.

(1) transcranial electromagnetic (TE) stimulation in the millimeter wavelength range (5.6-7.1 mm) can suppress the development of the active avoidance reflex with a painful reinforcement in rats; and (2) TE stimulation after intraperitonal injection of the blocking agents for serotonergic receptors has no effect on the development of the studied reflex.

transcranial millimeter-wave irradiation of the brain of rats inhibits the development of an avoidance conditioned reflex with painful reinforcement, and that it does not influence the retention of the acquired reflex.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of transcranially applied electromagnetic radiation on the development of a conditioned reflex with painful reinforcement.
the influence of transcranian electromagnetic brain stimulation on the formation of conditioned avoidance reflex in laboratory rats.
the possibility of the use of electromagnetic radiation in the treatment of mental diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

transcranial stimulation of the brain with low-frequency electromagnetic radiation leads to the inhibition of the development of an avoidance conditioned reflex with painful reinforcement, which is associated with a decrease in the formation of temporal binding of the studied reflex.
the electromagnetic radiation in the mm range, modulated as a sequence of low-frequency pulses has an inhibitory effect on the development of conditioned active avoidance reflex in laboratory rats.
electromagnetic brain stimulation is not a reliable method of influence on the brain activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
transcranial stimulation with millimeter electromagnetic radiation is a promising method for studying the neurophysiological basis of conditioned reflex development.
electromagnetic stimulation of the brain is an effective means of influencing on the formation of active avoidance reflexes.

the electromagnetic radiation of the millimeter range, modulated as a low-frequency pulse, is able to suppress the formation of conditioned reflexes with painful reinforcement in the case when the brain of the experimental animals is subjected to irradiation during the formation of the conditioned reflex.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of millimeter electromagnetic radiation as a noninvasive tool to study brain functions is promising.
the use of electromagnetic stimulation of the brain can be used to suppress the formation of conditioned reflexes in the process of learning.
transcranial stimulation can influence the development of conditioned reflexes in animals.
